reasoning: The Acme Bank policy fragment (ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 §5) explicitly requires a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment that includes “Fairness and bias considerations,” which is the same underlying obligation (mitigating bias) as Article 15(4). However, the fragment only addresses bias considerations at pre-deployment and does not specify requirements for AI systems that continue learning in production. Missing elements relative to Article 15(4) include: (1) explicit design requirements to eliminate or reduce feedback-loop risk where biased outputs influence future inputs, (2) post-deployment monitoring for biased feedback effects, (3) controls for ongoing/continuous learning (e.g., constraints on automated retraining, validation of new training data, human-in-the-loop approval), and (4) remediation/rollback procedures if feedback-induced bias is detected. The inventory and scope fragments (ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 §§3 and 2) show coverage of production systems but do not address these continuous-learning/feedback-loop controls. A human Compliance Analyst should review and confirm whether the policy must be supplemented to cover these missing lifecycle controls.

retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Before any AI system is deployed to production, the owning business unit must
complete a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment covering:

- Intended purpose and use cases
- Data sources and data quality
- Known limitations of the model or system
- Fairness and bias considerations
- Sign-off from the AIGC for high-impact systems

All AI systems must be registered in the Acme Bank AI System Inventory prior to
deployment, with the following minimum metadata: system name, business owner,
intended purpose, data sources, and deployment date.

Applies to all AI systems used in production, including those developed in-house
and those procured from third parties, across all business lines.
